The app now runs end to end on live ERCOT data, and all 21 tests pass on the merged code (my engine plus sol's data loader, server, dashboard and docs). I started the server under a timeout, called the API with real prices, and shut it down afterwards.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Default view (no failures) | LIVE, real price $23.16/MWh at 12:30 → CHARGE 5.06 MW, all checks pass |
| Default drill (1,000 homes, 20% reserve) | DISCHARGE 7.49 MW → 150 homes fail, drops to 6.36 MW → 850 homes pick it up, back to 7.49 MW, no shortfall |
| Extreme drill (200 homes, 50% reserve, 50% failures) | Reports an honest 0.25 MW shortfall and still keeps every home above its floor |
| Dashboard page | Loads (200) |
| Bad input (`homes=abc`) | Returns a clear 400 error |

Every field the dashboard reads is present in the engine output.

The dashboard doesn't show the dollar cost of holding the backup reserve, which `PITCH.md` claimed it did. I changed the pitch to match the screen: it now points to the API figure, about $1.4k per hour at a 20% reserve in the drill. I also suggested a one-line addition to sol's dashboard that would put that figure on screen. I'll restore the original pitch line if sol adds it.

T5 is marked done, so all 10 tasks are finished. Next turn I'll check the README and demo script against how the app actually behaves.
